thread:
mike_seller: Hey team — Acme demo is tomorrow AM and their POC is failing with 403 on /v1/generate. Can someone triage? They tested from our sandbox.

jamie_engineer: Can you paste the curl you used + full response body? 403 could be header or token scope.

mike_seller: Sure — curl they ran:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXX' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"rwx-13b","input":"Hello"}'
```
Response body: `{"error":{"code":403,"message":"Forbidden: invalid project binding"}}`

irina_sre: That message usually means the key isn't bound to the project header or token claims lack the required inference scope. Did they include any project/org header?

mike_seller: They only sent the Authorization header (above). No X-Project or X-Org header.

devon_support: If they're using project-scoped keys, we require X-Project-ID. Otherwise token must have a project claim that matches the request. Two quick checks: 1) decode the JWT to inspect claims; 2) check token scopes.

jamie_engineer: Yep. Ask them to run:
```
printf '%s' "$TOKEN" | cut -d'.' -f2 | base64 -d | jq .
```
That will show claims. Post the `scopes` and `project` fields.

mike_seller: I got the decoded claim from their team: `{"sub":"svc:acme-demo","project":"acme-demo","scopes":["embeddings:read"]}`

devon_support: There's the problem — scope is only embeddings:read. Model inferencing requires `inference:invoke`. We'll need to reissue a token with the proper scope or use a key bound to the project that includes inference.

sara_security: Quick security note for the customer — if we reissue keys, confirm whether they want keys rotated to their KMS. Also mention in the security questionnaire that PII won't be logged and audit logs are retained for 90 days by default.

jamie_engineer: I pushed a temporary remediation: created a service key with scopes ["inference:invoke","embeddings:read"] and bound to project=acme-demo. @devon_support can you rotate theirs and share new credentials to the customer secure channel?

devon_support: On it. Creating key now and setting delivery method to secure link. Will also set X-Project-ID example in their client. Ticket created: INC-4532.

deploy_bot: [bot] Key creation event: service_key_ghr9 created by devon_support for project acme-demo (expires: 30d). Ticket: INC-4532.

mike_seller: After they used the new key + added header `X-Project-ID: acme-demo` they still saw 401 once.

jamie_engineer: 401 suggests signature/format or using a short-lived key that expired. Ask them to run this quick check:
```
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <NEW_KEY>' \
  -H 'X-Project-ID: acme-demo' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"rwx-13b","input":"ping"}'
```
Share the `WWW-Authenticate` header if present.

mike_seller: They pasted back: `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error=\"invalid_token\", error_description=\"signature verification failed\"`

irina_sre: That indicates they might be copying the key incorrectly or there's an extra whitespace/URL-encoding issue (common with CLI env vars). Ask them to `echo -n "$TOKEN" | wc -c` and confirm length. Also verify there aren't extra quotes when setting env var.

devon_support: I asked them to set the key as `export REDWOOD_KEY=sk_live_XXX` (no surrounding extra quotes in client). They retried and got 200.

mike_seller: ✅ They confirm: generation now returns 200 and streaming works. Demo on track. Thanks all.

mike_seller: One customer question left — will they need Dedicated for lower latency on inference? They're currently on trial. Any short guidance for pricing?

devon_support: For demos, hosted should be fine. If they move to heavy production with strict latency SLOs, suggest Dedicated (reserved GPU pools). I sent a short cost estimate and next steps to your DM, @mike_seller.

sara_security: Also shared the excerpt for the security questionnaire about key management and audit logs. Send it to the customer if they ask.

jamie_engineer: Closing notes: root cause = token had insufficient scopes + missing X-Project-ID; secondary issue = token copy had whitespace causing signature errors. Documented in INC-4532. :white_check_mark:
